thread:
liz_support: Heads up — ACME is seeing a big spike in 503s on hosted inference since ~09:12 UTC. Customer says requests time out and some return 500. Reporting auth/timeouts + high latencies.
jon_oncall: saw the alert. Upstream runner crash rate jumped, multiple container restarts on gpu pool in us-west-2. Node drain triggered.
deploy-bot: ALERT: upstream-runner-abrupt-exit spike detected (metric: runner.exit_rate) — 6823456789
carol_sre: grabbing logs from the affected pods now. early tail shows repeated faults: `terminate signal 11` and nvml reports OOM on allocation. attaching excerpt:```
[2026-03-17T09:12:05Z] infer-runner[pid=4123]: segfault at 0 ip ...
[2026-03-17T09:12:06Z] nvml: OutOfMemory when allocating 2048MB for kv_prefetch
[2026-03-17T09:12:06Z] infer-runner[pid=4123]: aborting due to GPU OOM
``` 
mike_engineer: that lines up with a prefetch surge during a model swap. We saw similar when prefetch parallelism + dynbatch changes interact. Can we check batch sizes hitting 32+?
liz_support: customer traffic pattern was a quick warmup — they increased context length and QPS queued up. they hit p95 spikes.
sara_csm: I forwarded the logs to ACME and asked for a short window to test fallbacks. they're reporting that retries sometimes succeed.
jon_oncall: mitigation options: (1) enable fallback routing to cpu-workers for that shard, (2) temporarily reduce prefetch parallelism and autoscale burst, (3) pin them to an older model variant without aggressive prefetch. Which do we want live?
carol_sre: immediate: flip fallback routing so requests go to smaller-capacity CPU runners while we stabilize GPU pool. command to run:```bash
rctl route set --service=infer --region=us-west-2 --policy fallback_cpu=true
``` That will stop new requests from hitting the failing pool. Also lowering prefetch parallelism: set env PREFETCH_PARALLEL=2 on the daemonset.
mike_engineer: I'll open a hotfix to cap prefetch concurrency and add a guard on model swap that throttles kvcache population. PR: https://git.internal/rw/infra/pull/1234 — test in staging.
liz_support: shared the fallback instruction with customer and asked them to retry. they confirmed a few successful requests but still see intermittent 500s.
sara_csm: customer asked about credits for the window. I'll log impact and start an SLO review.
jon_oncall: I'm isolating the most noisy nodes, collecting full heap dumps and corefiles, and will repro with the model and a synthetic workload in staging. posting repro steps here shortly.
carol_sre: note for postmortem — root cause likely interaction between kv-prefetch growth during model swap and a new dynbatch heuristic; memory accounting didn't throttle prefetch. add to timeline.
mike_engineer: added a temporary guard in the runtime to reject prefetch requests if free_gpu_mem < 3GB. deploy in canary now.
liz_support: thanks team. keeping ACME patched and tracking. will update thread once we have stable metrics and rollback plan. :thumbsup:
deploy-bot: ACTION: canary deploy started for infra hotfix pr-1234 on us-west-2
jon_oncall: copying results to incident doc and I'll ping oncall channel when stable.
carol_sre: follow-up: we'll run a job to trim kvcache sizes overnight for affected nodes to free memory and prevent repeated OOM churn.
liz_support: recorded customer impact and ETA for SRE/ENG follow-ups. closing interim escalation, will reopen if errors reappear.
